title: Deadlines on Drug Coverage Requests, Exceptions and Redeterminations under a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan
content:
Every drug coverage request the plan accepts on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan receives a decision, and its deadline is fixed by whether the request is standard or expedited and by whether it is an initial determination, an exception or a redetermination. The decision deadlines of each plan are the ones certified for the plan held.

## Counting the deadline

The plan gives its decision no later than the decision deadline counted from the time the plan received the request, or from the time the prescriber's supporting statement arrived where the request is an exception. Hours are counted as full 24-hour periods from the recorded receipt time, calendar days are counted from the day after the receipt date with every day of the week counting, a decision given exactly on the deadline is in time, and the two units are never mixed.

| When the decision is given | Whether it is in time |
| --- | --- |
| Before the deadline falls | in time |
| Exactly on the deadline | in time |
| After the deadline has fallen | out of time |

## The conditions on particular kinds of request

1. A formulary or tiering exception cannot be decided without the prescriber's supporting statement, and the clock for an exception starts when that statement arrives rather than when the member first asked.
2. A request is expedited where waiting the standard time could seriously harm the member's life, health or ability to regain maximum function, and a prescriber's request for expedition is always granted.
3. A tiering exception may never move a drug to the specialty tier's cost share, and a request to do so is dismissed with the reason explained rather than silently denied.

## What follows a decision, and what follows none

Where the plan does not decide by the deadline the request goes to the independent review entity automatically, and the member is told so without having to ask.

An approval holds good until its approved through date, and a member whose approval is running out is told before it lapses rather than discovering it at the counter.
